statements.text: This bill recognizes the danger that AI can pose when employed by terrorists who seek to harm our homeland. [...] It requires the Department of Homeland Security to analyze incidents where foreign terrorist organizations have used or attempted to use generative AI to spread violent extremist messaging and to recruit, radicalize, or plot attacks.
statements.context: Floor speech in the U.S. House of Representatives advocating for H.R. 1736, the Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act.

statements.text:
Classification cannot be a shield to avoid public accountability.

Allowing the government – especially this government – to use AI tools for “any lawful purpose” without independent oversight is an invitation to weaponize them.

Congress must pass serious legislation on AI to protect Americans’ privacy, safety, and civil liberties from government overreach.
statements.quoted: Google reportedly signed a deal with the US Department of Defense to provide AI models for classified work, joining OpenAI and xAI in similar agreements https://t.co/38N3wog7E1 https://t.co/3kVPCTK50e

statements.text:
Half of American renters spend over 30% of their income on housing.

A major culprit? Algorithms that allow landlords to coordinate rent hikes and kill competition.

As NYS continues to fight these practices in court, I’m proud to be leading 56 Dems, alongside @RepBeccaB and @RepChuyGarcia, in demanding the FTC crack down nationwide on companies like RealPage that use AI to facilitate this rental price-fixing.

This 80-year-old STILL does not use email — his staff prints things for him to read — yet we are supposed to have faith that he alone can protect us from the escalating dangers of AI. 

This is not a joke. Congress must act now. https://t.co/3OFritasPF
